nodes.summary: For every list $L$ with entries in an additive monoid, the aggregate of the segment tree built from $L$ equals the sum of the entries of $L$, taken from left to right.
nodes.title: Aggregate of a built segment tree

nodes.summary: If $t$ is a valid segment tree with values in an additive monoid, then the aggregate of $t$ equals the sum of the leaf values of $t$, taken from left to right.
nodes.title: Aggregate of a valid segment tree

nodes.summary: Let $L = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a list with entries in an additive monoid, let $i < n$, and let $y$ be an element of the monoid. Applying the point update at index $i$ with value $y$ to the segment tree built from $L$ gives a tree whose aggregate is the sum, taken from left to right, of the list obtained from $L$ by replacing $x_i$ with $y$.
nodes.title: Aggregate after a point update of a built segment tree

nodes.summary: The aggregate of a segment tree with values in an additive monoid is $0$ for the empty tree, $x$ for a single leaf with value $x$, and the aggregate cached at the root for an internal node.
nodes.title: Aggregate of a segment tree

nodes.summary: The segment tree built from a list $L$ with entries in an additive monoid is the empty tree if $L$ is empty, and a single leaf with value $x$ if $L = (x)$. If $L$ has length $n \ge 2$, it is the internal node whose left child is the tree built from the first $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ entries of $L$, whose right child is the tree built from the remaining entries, and which caches the aggregate of the left child plus the…
nodes.title: Building a segment tree from a list

nodes.summary: If $t$ is a valid segment tree with values in an additive monoid, then the length of the list of leaf values of $t$, read from left to right, equals the size of $t$.
nodes.title: Size of a valid segment tree

nodes.summary: Let $L = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a list with entries in an additive monoid and let $l, r$ be natural numbers. The range query over $[l, r)$ on the segment tree built from $L$ returns $\sum_{l \le k < \min(r, n)} x_k$, the sum taken in increasing order of $k$; it is $0$ when $\min(r, n) \le l$.
nodes.title: Range queries on a built segment tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a valid segment tree with values in an additive monoid, let $(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be its leaf values from left to right, and let $l, r$ be natural numbers. The range query over $[l, r)$ on $t$ returns $\sum_{l \le k < \min(r, n)} x_k$, the sum taken in increasing order of $k$; it is $0$ when $\min(r, n) \le l$.
nodes.title: Correctness of range queries on a valid segment tree

nodes.summary: Let $L = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a list with entries in an additive monoid, let $i < n$, let $y$ be an element of the monoid, and let $L'$ be the list obtained from $L$ by replacing $x_i$ with $y$, with entries $x'_0, \dots, x'_{n-1}$. Apply the point update at index $i$ with value $y$ to the segment tree built from $L$. For all natural numbers $l, r$, the range query over $[l, r)$ on the result returns…
nodes.title: Range queries after a point update of a built segment tree

nodes.summary: For a segment tree $t$ with values in an additive monoid and natural numbers $l, r$, the range query over $[l, r)$, with positions counted from the start of the segment of $t$, is defined recursively. On the empty tree it is $0$. On a leaf with value $x$ it is $x$ if $l = 0 < r$, and $0$ otherwise. On an internal node with cached aggregate $a$, cached size $s$ and children $t_1, t_2$, it is $0$ if $r \le l$ or…
nodes.title: Range query on a segment tree

nodes.summary: A segment tree with values in $\alpha$ is either empty, a leaf holding a value in $\alpha$, or an internal node holding a cached segment aggregate in $\alpha$, a cached segment length in $\mathbb{N}$, a left child and a right child, both segment trees.
nodes.title: Segment tree

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ with entries in an additive monoid, the segment tree built from $xs$ has size equal to the length of $xs$.
nodes.title: Size of a built segment tree

nodes.summary: For every segment tree $t$ over an additive monoid, every index $i$ and every value $y$, the point update of $t$ at $i$ with $y$ has the same size as $t$.
nodes.title: Point update preserves the size of a segment tree

nodes.summary: The size of a segment tree is $0$ for the empty tree, $1$ for a leaf, and, for an internal node, the segment length cached at that node.
nodes.title: Size of a segment tree

nodes.summary: For every segment tree $t$ and every list $acc$, the accumulator traversal of $t$ starting from $acc$ returns the leaf list of $t$ followed by $acc$.
nodes.title: Accumulator traversal prepends the leaf list

nodes.summary: Given a segment tree and a list $acc$, the accumulator traversal returns $acc$ for the empty tree, the list $acc$ with $x$ prepended for a leaf with value $x$, and, for an internal node with left child $L$ and right child $R$, the traversal of $L$ starting from the result of the traversal of $R$ starting from $acc$.
nodes.title: Accumulator traversal of a segment tree

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ with entries in an additive monoid, the leaf list of the segment tree built from $xs$ is $xs$.
nodes.title: Building a segment tree preserves the list

nodes.summary: For every internal node of a segment tree, with any cached aggregate, any cached length, left child $L$ and right child $R$, its leaf list is the leaf list of $L$ followed by the leaf list of $R$.
nodes.title: Leaf list of an internal node

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ with entries in an additive monoid, every index $i$ smaller than the length of $xs$ and every value $y$, the leaf list of the segment tree built from $xs$, after the point update at $i$ with $y$, is $xs$ with its entry at position $i$ (counting from $0$) replaced by $y$.
nodes.title: Point update of a built segment tree

nodes.summary: For every valid segment tree $t$ over an additive monoid, every index $i$ at least the size of $t$ and every value $y$, the point update of $t$ at $i$ with $y$ has the same leaf list as $t$.
nodes.title: Out-of-range point update leaves the leaf list unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a valid segment tree over an additive monoid and let $i$ be a natural number less than the size of $t$. Then for every value $y$, the leaf list of the point update of $t$ at $i$ with $y$ is the leaf list of $t$ with its entry at position $i$ (counting from $0$) replaced by $y$.
nodes.title: Leaf list after an in-range point update

nodes.summary: The leaf list of a segment tree is the list of its leaf values from left to right: the empty list for the empty tree, $[x]$ for a leaf with value $x$, and the leaf list of the left child followed by the leaf list of the right child for an internal node.
nodes.title: Leaf list of a segment tree

nodes.summary: If $t$ is a valid segment tree over an additive monoid, then for every natural number $i$ and every value $y$, the point update of $t$ at $i$ with $y$ is valid.
nodes.title: Point update preserves validity

nodes.summary: The point update of a segment tree over an additive monoid at an index $i \in \mathbb{N}$, relative to the tree's segment, with a value $y$ is defined recursively. The empty tree stays empty. A leaf becomes a leaf with value $y$ if $i = 0$ and is unchanged otherwise. At an internal node with left child $L$ and right child $R$: if $i$ is less than the size of $L$, then $L$ is replaced by its point update at $i$ with…
nodes.title: Point update of a segment tree

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over an additive monoid, the segment tree built from $xs$ is valid.
nodes.title: Built segment trees are valid

nodes.summary: Validity of a segment tree over an additive monoid is defined inductively: the empty tree and every leaf are valid, and an internal node with valid left child $L$ and valid right child $R$ is valid when its cached aggregate is the aggregate of $L$ plus the aggregate of $R$ and its cached length is the size of $L$ plus the size of $R$. Here the aggregate and size of the empty tree are $0$ and $0$, of a leaf with…
nodes.title: Valid segment trees

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
